title: Support-tier mix TCO playbook — on‑prem vs VPC
summary: Working spreadsheet and narrative that evaluates marginal and portfolio-level TCO for mixing support tiers (Standard / Premium / Platinum) across On‑Prem and VPC private deployments. Focus: quantify how support bundle mix affects 1/3/5‑year unit economics, break‑even, and recommended bundle compositions for small-mid-large enterprise customers.
scope_and_objectives: Create a repeatable scenario generator that: 1) models infra (CapEx vs Opex), licensing, and support costs; 2) computes NPV and payback; 3) runs sensitivity on support headcount and incident rate; 4) produces bundle mix recommendations to hit target gross margin and payback thresholds.
assumptions: On‑prem CapEx amortized over 36 months; straight‑line depreciation
VPC infra billed monthly as Opex (estimated cloud overlay + managed infra margin)
Base model licensing = $X per GPU-equivalent (placeholder to be parameterized)
Support tiers: Standard (SLAs, email only), Premium (24/7 + 2hr on-call), Platinum (dedicated TAM + RPO/RTO), with step increases in cost and expected ARR uplift
Support staff fully burdened cost = $180k/year (base), escalation factor for Premium/Platinum time allocation
Target customer ARR bands: Small=$120k, Mid=$850k, Large=$4.5M (used for sizing economics)
Incident rate baseline = 4 incidents/customer/yr; Premium reduces measurable impact by ~30% (operational assumption)
Model currently excludes taxes, fringe benefits beyond burdened support cost, and reseller margins — add later if needed

calculation_notes: Quick formulas in sheet: total_year1 = infra_year1 + licensing_year1 + support_cost_year1. NPV_3yr = sum_{t=1..3} cashflow_t / (1+0.08)^{t-1}; cashflows include support revenue uplift assumptions. Payback_months uses cumulative cashflow crossing initial outlay for OnPrem (CapEx) and initial 3 months for VPC because of monthly billing. Sensitivity lever: support_headcount_per_100_customers and incident_cost_per_incident are primary knobs.
sensitivity_matrix_outline: Primary axes: x-axis = %customers on Premium (0-50%), y-axis = incident rate (2-8 incidents/yr). Cells show delta NPV and delta payback relative to all-standard baseline. Secondary runs: vary support fully-burdened cost ±20% and cloud infra unit cost ±15%.
sample_findings: For Mid customers, moving 30% of customers to Premium increases support run-rate ~60% but shortens payback by ~1-2 months due to reduced incident-related revenue churn assumptions (model sensitive to ARR uplift attribution).
On‑prem shows ~1.8x higher cash outlay in year 1 vs VPC for equivalent capacity; however NPV over 3 years can be lower for On‑prem when utilization > 70% and amortization windows are fully utilized.
Platinum tiers (dedicated TAM) only justify the incremental cost for Large accounts (ARR > $2.5M) unless we price a cross-sell uplift into the bundle aggressively.
Support headcount is the dominant recurring cost for Premium/Platinum economics; reducing escalations via auto-remediation reduces long-term marginal cost the most (automation lever recommended).
key_recommendations: Introduce a recommended 'Hybrid Support Mix' for Mid customers: Standard 60% / Premium 30% / Platinum 10% — target price points to preserve ~40% gross margin after support labor and infra amortization.
Price Premium so that per-customer support margin covers incremental support FTE burden (target $/FTE demand coverage = $300k of ARR per FTE of premium load).
For On‑prem deals with expected utilization < 60% over 36 months, prefer VPC offering with a migration discount to keep cash conversion favorable for customers.
Invest in runbooks and automated runbook execution to lower effective incident cost and thus widen the margin of Premium offerings without raising price.
Create a simple customer-facing calculator (embed in proposal template) that shows payback and 3-yr NPV under selected mix options — reduces negotiation friction for on‑prem quotes.
